articles.title: Biofuels Made from Waste and Turning Alcohol to Jet Fuel
articles.raw_title: Biofuels Made from Waste and Turning Alcohol to Jet Fuel
articles.snippet: Biofuels are necessary in helping to decarbonize the entire transport sector, from which around 20% of global emissions are generated. From bioethanol for...
articles.text:
Biofuels Made from Waste and Turning Alcohol to Jet Fuel
Biofuels are necessary in helping to decarbonize the entire transport sector, from which around 20% of global emissions are generated. From bioethanol for cars to SAF for planes, the entire fuel market is being re-evaluated in a light of sustainability. IDTechEx's portfolio of Sustainability Research Reports and Subscriptions covers an entire range of initiatives which aim to significantly lower harmful emissions.
Bioethanol, biodiesel, and advanced biofuels
Although electric vehicles are one solution to decarbonizing road transport covered in IDTechEx's portfolio of Electric Vehicles Research Reports and Subscriptions, for the wider transportation landscape including aviation and shipping, electrification is not a feasible option. Low-carbon fuels, many of which can be drop-in fuels requiring minimal infrastructure changes, will therefore be a better-suited alternative. Bioethanol and biodiesel are also already used globally for cars in gasoline and diesel blends, to reduce the number of harmful emissions created from existing combustion engine vehicles. IDTechEx's report, "Sustainable Biofuels & E-Fuels Market 2026-2036: Technologies, Players, Forecasts", goes into further detail.
Bioethanol is mostly created from sugarcane, while biodiesel is traditionally made from vegetable oils, meaning both are created from natural feedstocks rather than coming from fossil fuels. However, one of the main issues with these feedstocks is the high land and water usage required in their production, which can come at the cost of deforestation and loss of biodiversity. Many traditional 1st generation biofuels are therefore also still responsible for a significant amount of greenhouse gas emissions. According to IDTechEx, government subsidies are now shifting more towards the production of advanced biofuels and e-fuels that generate even less emissions, and as a result, scalability of 1st generation biofuels is currently limited.
Advanced biofuels encompass 2nd, 3rd, and 4th generation biofuels. 2nd generation biofuels are created from lignocellulose or waste biomass and vegetable oils, as to recycle pre-used materials and to not demand excess land usage, while 3rd generation biofuels are expected to be made from algae, and 4th generation from genetically engineered microorganisms, algae, or even captured CO2. IDTechEx's report, "Industrial Biomanufacturing 2027-2037: Technologies, Markets, Players, Forecasts", report covers a whole range of biomanufacturing routes and applications including fuels.
SAF, HEFA, and alcohol-to-jet fuel
Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) for planes is one market seeing significant growth and investment. SAF is created via the HEFA (hydrotreated esters and fatty acids) route, which sees oils and other waste materials treated with hydrogen to remove oxygen and collect hydrocarbons which are chemically the same as regular diesel or kerosene. Globally, there is reportedly a few million tonnes of HEFA- SAF capacity a year, with IDTechEx forecasting the global SAF market to reach US$50 billion in 2036.
Alcohol-to-jet is an alternative biofuel pathway, which sees ethanol or methanol being upgraded to hydrocarbon fuels, which can then be blended with regular jet fuel. This process sees ethanol and methanol undergoing dehydration, oligomerization, hydrogenation and isomerization, and finally fractional distillation. Details of these processes can be found in IDTechEx's "Sustainable Biofuels & E-Fuels Market" report.
Many companies have already begun commercial operation of alcohol-to-jet fuel which IDTechEx states will pave the way for even bigger SAF production capabilities. One of LanzaJet's facilities has been reported to produce 9 million gallons of SAF and 1 million gallons of renewable diesel a year, highlighting the great scope for further growth within the market and encouraging many other companies to follow suit.
For more information on the biofuel market and other sustainable initiatives within the transport sector, visit IDTechEx's portfolio of Sustainability Research Reports and Subscriptions for the latest developments.

articles.title: Maersk completes first 100% bioethanol bunkering in US
articles.raw_title: Maersk completes first 100% bioethanol bunkering in US
articles.snippet: Maersk has completed the first bunkering of a vessel with 100% bioethanol in the US, using fuel supplied by American producer POET.
articles.text:
Maersk has completed the first bunkering of a vessel with 100% bioethanol in the US, using fuel supplied by American producer POET.
The trial took place in Houston and marks another step in Maersk’s testing of bioethanol across its dual-fuel fleet.
POET, which describes itself as the world’s largest bioethanol producer, supplied the plant-based fuel. Kirby Corporation supported the marine bunkering operation and fuel transportation, while the Port of Houston provided port coordination and infrastructure. The US Coast Guard supported the regulatory requirements needed for the operation.
“Bioethanol has the potential to contribute meaningfully to the future energy mix for shipping,” said Emma Mazhari, Maersk’s vice president energy markets.
She added that bioethanol can provide “another scalable, lower-emission fuel option” while giving the industry greater flexibility as it moves towards lower-carbon fuels.
POET produces more than 3bn gallons of bioethanol annually across 35 bioprocessing facilities and argues that existing production, transport and distribution infrastructure could support wider use in shipping.
Jeff Broin, POET’s founder and CEO, said the Houston trial demonstrated the potential to connect US agricultural production directly with marine fuel demand.
“Seeing American-made bioethanol move from the farm to a container ship in one of the nation’s largest ports is an exciting moment for our industry,” Broin said.
The company said the trial showed bioethanol can move beyond its traditional road-fuel role into large-scale maritime applications.

articles.title: Maersk performs in Houston the first supply of 100% bioethanol to a container ship in the US
articles.raw_title: Maersk performs in Houston the first supply of 100% bioethanol to a container ship in the US
articles.snippet: Maersk has completed in Houston the first commercial operation of ship-to-ship supply of 100% ethanol to an oceangoing container ship in...
articles.text:
Maersk has completed in Houston the first commercial operation of ship-to-ship supply of 100% ethanol to an oceangoing container ship in the United States. The fuel, produced from US corn, has been supplied by POET as part of the program with which the Danish shipping company analyzes the incorporation of different fuels into its dual-fuel engine fleet.
The supply has been made to the Tangier Maersk, a 9,000 TEU container ship incorporated this year into the company's fleet and equipped with a dual-fuel propulsion system ready to use methanol. The trial is supported by the existing similarities between methanol and ethanol, both alcohols, which allows studying the use of the latter in systems initially designed for the use of methanol as an alternative fuel.
The operation has involved the participation of various US companies and agencies. POET has supplied the bioethanol from plant sources, while Kirby Corporation has been responsible for the transportation of the fuel and support for the maritime supply operation. The Port of Houston has provided port coordination and the necessary infrastructure, and the US Coast Guard has intervened in the regulatory requirements associated with the procedure.
For Maersk, the test allows obtaining information under commercial conditions regarding aspects related to fuel operations, supply infrastructures, sourcing, and logistics chain organization. The company considers that the development of this alternative will also depend on factors such as product availability, the regulatory framework, and the readiness of various agents in the maritime chain.
“Bioethanol has the potential to contribute meaningfully to the future energy mix for shipping,” said Emma Mazhari, Vice President of Energy Markets at Maersk. According to the company's official, bioethanol may constitute another low-emission fuel option capable of achieving a larger scale and providing more flexibility to the maritime industry in the process of reducing its carbon footprint.
POET, based in South Dakota, produces over 3 billion gallons of bioethanol per year through a network of 35 bioprocessing facilities. The company believes that existing production in the United States, along with the storage, transportation, and distribution networks already developed for this fuel, can facilitate its entry into the maritime market.
The United States is the world's largest producer of ethanol, followed by Brazil, and both countries account for around 80% of global production. The availability of a developed industry is one of the elements that Maersk is analyzing when studying this alternative for its fleet, along with the technical compatibility with vessels prepared to consume alcohol-based fuels.
Jeff Broin, founder and CEO of POET, has linked the Houston operation with the possibility of connecting US agricultural production with the demand for maritime transport fuels. The company believes that the trial allows transporting bioethanol from a market historically linked to land transport towards larger-scale maritime applications.
The trial with the Tangier Maersk is part of a program previously initiated by Maersk on board the Laura Maersk. During a first phase conducted in 2025, the shipping company used a mixture consisting of 10% ethanol and 90% e-methanol to check its integration into the fuel system and analyze aspects such as ignition, combustion, lubricity, corrosion, and emissions.
After that first test, Maersk subsequently raised the ethanol proportion to a mixture of 50% with methanol and continued its trials with higher concentrations. The program has also included operations with the Antonia Maersk, within the analysis that the company conducts on the possibility of using different alcohols in its dual-fuel fleet.
The Tangier Maersk belongs to a new series of medium-sized container ships ordered by Maersk with a nominal capacity of about 9,000 TEU and dual-fuel systems prepared for methanol. Its incorporation expands the number of vessels in the shipping company capable of operating with alternative fuels in addition to conventional marine fuels.
The company maintains a strategy based on studying different energy solutions instead of relying on a single fuel. Besides methanol and ethanol, Maersk is working with other options to reduce emissions from its maritime operations. In the case of bioethanol, the tests developed so far seek to determine its technical behavior on board and the necessary conditions to have supply chains capable of meeting its potential commercial use in different ports.

articles.title: Ogun-Osun river basin, NNPC biofuels sign MoU for €256m bioethanol plant
articles.raw_title: Ogun-Osun river basin, NNPC biofuels sign MoU for €256m bioethanol plant
articles.snippet: The Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority and 3D NNPC Biofuels have signed an MoU to establish a €256m bioethanol plant in Lagos State.
articles.text:
The Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority and 3D NNPC Biofuels Limited have signed a Memorandum of Understanding for the establishment of a €256m bioethanol plant in the Itokin area of Lagos State and the cultivation of cassava on 15,000 hectares of arable land across Lagos, Ogun, Osun and Oyo states.
The agreement, signed on Tuesday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, will see the Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority provide 200 hectares of land at its Itokin project site for the construction of the plant.
The authority will also make available 15,000 hectares of arable land from its land bank for large-scale cassava cultivation to provide feedstock for the facility.
Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority, Adedeji Ashiru, described the agreement as a major step towards strengthening Nigeria’s energy and food security.
Ashiru said the project would also support industrialisation, create jobs and unlock the economic potential of underutilised government assets.
He said, “It is with great joy and a profound sense of history that I welcome you all to this epoch-making occasion: the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding between the Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority and 3D NNPC Biofuels Limited for the establishment of a bioethanol fuel plant.
“Today is not just an MOU signing; today, we are planting the seed for Nigeria’s energy future, food security and industrial revolution.”
According to him, the partnership would involve ORBDA providing land, water resources, community support and an enabling environment, while 3D NNPC Biofuels Limited would provide technical expertise, funding, technology and off-taker assurance.
He said the project aligned with the Federal Government’s drive to promote food security, alternative energy sources and wealth creation through the commercialisation of public assets.
The ORBDA boss said the bioethanol plant would produce renewable bioethanol for blending with Premium Motor Spirit, adding that the project would help reduce the country’s carbon footprint and conserve foreign exchange spent on fuel imports.
He said the project would also establish a large-scale outgrower scheme for cassava farmers.
“Second, food security and industrialisation. The cultivation of 15,000 hectares of cassava will not only feed the plant, but will create a massive outgrower scheme that will empower thousands of farmers, women, and youth in our host communities.
“From land preparation to planting, harvesting, transportation, processing, and plant operation, this project is projected to create over 100,000 direct and indirect jobs for Nigerians.
“It will interest the public that this project is valued at 256 million euros. It is huge; I must say at this point that Mr President, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, is a visionary leader. He saw this ahead, and today, it is becoming a reality.
“On behalf of the board and management of ORBDA, I want to assure our partners that we are fully committed to this project. We will provide the land, we will provide the community support, we will provide the water resources and the enabling environment to ensure this project succeeds on time and at scale,” Ashiru said.
On his part, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of 3D NNPC Biofuels Limited, Patrick Azi, said the company chose to partner with ORBDA after assessing the readiness of the 12 River Basin Development Authorities in the country to implement the Federal Government’s renewable energy and agricultural development agenda.
Azi said the authority was selected because of its coverage of four states in the South-West, availability of arable land and irrigation facilities, as well as the region’s strong cassava production base.
He said, “When we look at it, we now find out that we have a friend who is visionary, who has passion in renewable energy and who has been in the renewable energy space over a period of time. We then decided to approach the Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority.”
The MD disclosed that the proposed processing plant would be located in Lagos State, while the project would draw on cassava production from farmers across the region.
He said the authority had the land, irrigation facilities, dams, extension workers and farmers required to support the project, adding that the partnership would bring the resources together into an integrated agricultural and industrial value chain.
Azi said the company would work with ORBDA to improve agricultural productivity by preparing the land, supporting farmers and improving their yields per hectare.
He explained that a reliable supply of cassava would be critical to the success of the bioethanol plant.
Azi also disclosed that NNPC holds a 25 per cent equity stake in the joint venture, describing the partnership as an opportunity to bring the national oil company’s presence closer to communities in the region.
He added that the partners would work towards developing the framework agreement and commencing the project within weeks, with a target of flagging off the project before the end of the year.

articles.title: EU rebuffs Ukraine's bid to renegotiate export quotas
articles.raw_title: EU rebuffs Ukraine's bid to renegotiate export quotas
articles.snippet: Kyiv sought increased access for bioethanol exports.
articles.text:
EU rebuffs Ukraine's bid to renegotiate export quotas
Kyiv sought increased access for bioethanol exports
The European Union does not plan to renegotiate export quotas with Ukraine, a European Commission spokesperson said on Tuesday, rebuffing Kyiv's request for additional trade access as Russian strikes strain its economy, reported Reuters.
Trading terms with Ukraine have become a sensitive issue in the EU after tariff-free and quota-free access granted to Kyiv at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 led to an influx of agricultural goods, angering European farmers.
The EU reintroduced quotas for products such as wheat, sugar and eggs last year in response to farmer protests.
But Ukraine has sought an increased quota for its bioethanol exports, produced from its massive grain harvests.
"We can confirm there are no discussions planned with Ukrainian counterparts to renegotiate export quotas," the Commission spokesperson said in an emailed statement.
Trade data so far "proves the fair and balanced nature" of revised quota volumes under an updated version of the agreement, the spokesperson added.
The current quotas, adopted last year, cut imports of Ukrainian wheat and sugar compared with the quota-free period earlier in the war, though they represented an increase compared with pre-war quota levels.
Intensifying Russian attacks have damaged Ukrainian infrastructure while choking its exports via the Black Sea, including crucial agricultural trade.
Global Ag Media notes the current quota system extends well beyond wheat, sugar and eggs. It also covers poultry, pork, beef, lamb, honey, butter and processed starch, among other agricultural products.

articles.title: TMU Advances Microbial Biotechnology
articles.raw_title: TMU Advances Microbial Biotechnology
articles.snippet: As the world searches for cleaner energy, safer food systems, and more sustainable materials, microbial biotechnology is emerging as a powerful solution.
articles.text:
Taipei Medical University
As the world searches for cleaner energy, safer food systems, and more sustainable materials, microbial biotechnology is emerging as a powerful solution. At Taipei Medical University (TMU), researchers are transforming microorganisms and bio-based materials into practical innovations with applications ranging from biofuel production to biomedical products and eco-friendly food packaging.
A research team led by Associate Professor Shin-Ping Lin from the School of Food Safety at TMU has achieved a series of impactful breakthroughs in bacterial cellulose (BC) applications and microbial fermentation optimization.
Supported by Taiwan’s National Science and Technology Council (NSTC), the team’s findings have been published in leading international journals, including Bioresource Technology (impact factor 9 in 2024), LWT – Food Science and Technology (impact factor 6.6 in 2024), Food Packaging and Shelf Life (impact factor 10.6 in 2024), and the International Journal of Biological Macromolecules (impact factor 8.5 in 2024). Together, these studies highlight TMU’s growing strength in sustainable bioengineering and translational food science.
Enhancing Biofuel Efficiency through Cold Plasma Detoxification
To address the persistent challenge of fermentation inhibitors generated during lignocellulosic hydrolysis, the team developed an innovative physical detoxification strategy for bioethanol production. By applying atmospheric cold plasma (ACP), key inhibitory compounds—including formic acid, acetic acid, hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), and furfural—were effectively degraded.
Under optimized conditions of 200 W for 25 minutes, ACP achieved complete removal of furfural and up to 80% degradation of HMF. This significantly enhanced fermentation performance, increasing the bioethanol productivity of Kluyveromyces marxianus from 0.25 to 0.65 g/L/h. Notably, the study also identified chicken meal as a cost-effective alternative nitrogen source, further improving the economic feasibility of bioethanol production.
Graphic abstract of ACP detoxification of agriculture waste for bioethanol production
Boosting Functional Biopolymer Production via Immobilized Fermentation
The team also established an advanced mycelium immobilization system to enhance the production of extracellular polysaccharides (EPS), compounds widely recognized for their therapeutic potential.
Through response surface methodology (RSM), EPS production in an alginate-based immobilized system increased by 90.2%. When scaled up in a bubble column bioreactor, yields reached 10.42 g/L, while the immobilized beads remained stable and reusable for at least three cycles.
Importantly, the produced EPS demonstrated strong antioxidant activity and antibacterial effects against Staphylococcus aureus, while exhibiting no signs of harming normal cells—highlighting its promise for biomedical and functional food applications.
Graphic abstract of optimized fermentation of Cordyceps militaris for extracellular polysaccharide production
Developing Smart and Sustainable Food Packaging Using Porous Bacterial Cellulose
Addressing both food spoilage and environmental concerns, the team engineered a novel active packaging material by modifying the structural properties of bacterial cellulose.
The researchers developed a foaming bacterial cellulose (FBC) film using foam templating combined with agar incorporation, creating a highly porous structure with excellent swelling capacity. The film was further functionalized with carvacrol, a natural antimicrobial compound, enabling controlled release behavior enhanced by the agar matrix.
In sea bass fillet preservation tests, the carvacrol-loaded FBC film significantly inhibited the growth of Shewanella putrefaciens, reduced lipid oxidation by 67.5%, and effectively delayed the accumulation of total volatile basic nitrogen (TVBN). These results demonstrate its strong potential as a sustainable alternative to conventional plastic-based food packaging.
Graphic abstract of agar altered foaming bacterial cellulose for food packaging application
Translating Microbial Technologies into Real-World Solutions
Together, these three studies from an integrated bioengineering pipeline—from fermentation optimization and high-value bioproduct generation to sustainable material applications. By advancing microbial technologies across energy, biomedical, and food preservation, Associate Professor Lin’s team demonstrates TMU’s capacity to translate fundamental research into innovative solutions that support sustainability, public health, and industrial applications.

articles.title: Maersk tests U.S. ethanol bunkering as shipping weighs alternative fuels
articles.raw_title: Maersk tests U.S. ethanol bunkering as shipping weighs alternative fuels
articles.snippet: Maersk has completed the first U.S. ship to ship commercial ethanol bunkering of a deep sea container vessel, using American corn ethanol aboard Tangier...
articles.text:
A.P. Moller Maersk has completed the first ship to ship commercial ethanol bunkering of a deep sea container vessel in the United States, using domestically produced corn ethanol aboard the Tangier Maersk.
The operation adds ethanol to the range of fuels being tested by major container carriers as the shipping industry looks for practical ways to reduce emissions while maintaining global vessel operations.
The fuel was supplied by U.S. bioethanol producer POET, which said the trial used 100% plant based bioethanol. Industry reports place the bunkering operation in Houston.
Tangier Maersk puts ethanol into commercial operation
The Tangier Maersk is an alcohol enabled dual fuel container vessel delivered in 2026. Maersk’s published vessel schedule lists the ship at 9,016 TEU nominal capacity and shows calls at Mobile and Houston during September.
Maersk said the operation was intended to provide practical information about fuel handling, infrastructure, sourcing and the supply chain needed to use ethanol in commercial shipping.
That distinction matters. A fuel may work technically in an engine, but operating it across international liner networks requires reliable production, storage, bunkering infrastructure and regulatory acceptance at multiple ports.
Ethanol already has a substantial production and distribution network in the United States, potentially giving it an infrastructure advantage compared with some newer marine fuel alternatives. POET said it supplied the ethanol used in the operation.
Maersk broadens its fuel testing
The latest bunkering follows earlier ethanol trials involving the Laura Maersk and Antonia Maersk, extending the carrier’s experience with ethanol across its alcohol capable fleet.
Maersk Regional President for North America Ditlev Blicher said the operation provided real world experience with alternative fuels and would help the company understand how lower emission supply chains could be developed at commercial scale.
The carrier has stressed, however, that technical compatibility alone will not determine whether ethanol develops into a significant marine fuel. Availability, regulation, infrastructure and operational readiness across the maritime supply chain will also determine whether widespread adoption is practical.
U.S. ethanol supply offers another marine fuel pathway
For U.S. ethanol producers, shipping could represent another potential outlet for an industry already operating at substantial scale.
POET described the trial as demonstrating how existing American ethanol production could connect with the marine fuel market. The company operates 35 production facilities and produces more than 3 billion gallons of bioethanol annually.
For container shipping, the significance lies less in a single bunkering operation than in whether ethanol can eventually be supplied consistently across major trade lanes. Deep sea vessels cannot depend on a fuel available at only a handful of ports.
The Tangier Maersk operation gives Maersk another commercial data point as it assesses which combination of alternative fuels can be supported by production capacity, port infrastructure and its expanding dual fuel fleet.

articles.title: Maersk and POET complete the first 100% bioethanol bunkering operation in the US
articles.raw_title: Maersk and POET complete the first 100% bioethanol bunkering operation in the US
articles.snippet: The first ever bunkering operation involving 100% bioethanol in the United States has been successfully completed at the Port of Houston, Texas (USA).
articles.text:
Maersk and POET complete the first 100% bioethanol bunkering operation in the US
29 September 2026
The first ever bunkering operation involving 100% bioethanol in the United States has been successfully completed at the Port of Houston, Texas (USA).
The key players are a container ship operated by the Danish group A.P. Moller – Maersk – the world’s second-largest container shipping company by fleet size – and the American company POET, the world’s largest producer of bioethanol, which has supplied the US-produced fuel.
The operation – as POET itself emphasises – marks the first refuelling of a vessel with 100% bioethanol carried out in the United States and forms part of the trial programme already successfully conducted by Maersk on its dual-fuel fleet. Bioethanol can offer shipping companies a low-carbon fuel, drawing on a well-established supply chain and infrastructure that is available globally.
“Seeing bioethanol produced in the United States make its way from the fields to a container ship at one of the country’s major ports is an exciting moment for our sector,” said Jeff Broin, founder and chief executive of POET. “Bioethanol is an abundant, cost-effective and clean solution for the maritime sector. This demonstrates what can be achieved when partners across the value chain work together to open up new markets for American agriculture.”.
Kirby Corporation supported the bunkering operations and the transport of fuel, whilst the Port of Houston provided the necessary infrastructure and coordinated port operations. The US Coast Guard assisted with the necessary regulatory compliance.
“Bioethanol has the potential to make a significant contribution to the future energy mix of maritime transport,” said Emma Mazhari, Vice President of Energy Markets at Maersk. “It can offer an additional, lower-emission fuel option that can be used on a large scale, as well as greater flexibility in the shipping industry’s transition towards lower-carbon fuels. This partnership with POET represents an important step towards assessing how to integrate bioethanol into marine fuel supply chains in the United States.”.
US bioethanol is already produced on a commercial scale: POET has an annual output of over 11.3 billion litres through its network of 35 biorefineries. The fuel benefits from well-established production, transport and distribution infrastructure and is available to markets around the world.
“For decades, bioethanol has proven to be a reliable fuel that can be used on a large scale in the world’s largest transport market,” said Broin. “We now have the opportunity to bring this same fuel, produced in the United States, to the global maritime market. As the world seeks practical solutions to reduce the carbon intensity and costs of transport, we should consider every technology and every market where bioethanol can create value. American agriculture is ready to help power this future.”.

articles.title: Why Maersk's Houston ethanol bunkering is really about risk?
articles.raw_title: Why Maersk's Houston ethanol bunkering is really about risk?
articles.snippet: A.P. Moller- Maersk has bunkered the containership Tangier Maersk with 100% U.S.-produced corn ethanol. Maersk describes the operation as the first…
articles.text:
A.P. Moller-Maersk has bunkered the containership Tangier Maersk with 100% U.S.-produced corn ethanol. Maersk describes the operation as the first ship-to-ship commercial ethanol bunkering of a deep-sea container vessel in the United States. POET, the bioethanol producer that supplied the fuel, says the bunkering took place in Houston and calls it the first U.S. marine bunkering operation using 100% bioethanol. Both "firsts" are company claims, so they are attributed here rather than independently verified.
The vessel has a nominal capacity of 9,016 TEU, was built in 2026, and is equipped with an alcohol-capable dual-fuel engine. It is the first in a series of new mid-sized dual-fuel ships entering Maersk's fleet.
Maersk's own framing is that the operation is about learning rather than about adopting ethanol as its fuel of choice. The company said the bunkering gave it practical experience with the infrastructure, sourcing, handling and supply-chain requirements of using ethanol at commercial scale. Ditlev Blicher, Maersk's regional president for North America, said the operation would provide real-world experience with alternative fuels in commercial shipping. Maersk has also not said that the Houston operation signals a shift away from methanol, so any reading of this event as "Maersk pivots to ethanol" goes beyond what the company has stated.
The Houston bunkering follows earlier Maersk trials aboard Laura Maersk and Antonia Maersk. Maersk began testing ethanol on Laura Maersk in 2025, initially with a blend of 10% ethanol and 90% e-methanol. It later moved to a 50-50 blend to examine whether engines developed for methanol could also operate on higher concentrations of ethanol. The source gives no details of the Antonia Maersk trials.
Read together, these steps show a progression from small ethanol shares toward pure ethanol. What distinguishes Houston is the setting: a U.S. port, a U.S. producer and a commercial ship-to-ship supply chain. Since the engine-compatibility questions were the focus of the earlier trials, a reasonable interpretation is that this operation tests logistics more than engineering, though Maersk has not put it in those terms.
Ethanol and methanol are both alcohols, which gives Maersk potential flexibility on vessels originally ordered around methanol propulsion. If methanol-designed engines can run on higher ethanol concentrations, the fleet gains a second fuel pathway without needing different ships. Maersk also noted that ethanol already has a large production base and established distribution infrastructure. Since availability is a recurring constraint for alternative marine fuels, a fuel with an existing industrial base can serve as a hedge against shortages elsewhere. That last point is analytical inference rather than a statement from the company.
Maersk said wider use of ethanol in shipping would depend on fuel availability, regulation and operational readiness. The Houston operation speaks most directly to operational readiness, and to a degree to availability, since it shows a supply chain can deliver the fuel to a deep-sea vessel. It does nothing to resolve the regulatory question. That is the notable gap: the practical demonstration is running ahead of policy certainty.
The ethanol trial sits within a widening approach to fuels. Maersk initially placed methanol at the center of its dual-fuel newbuilding program. It is now examining a broader mix that includes ethanol and biomethane, while keeping other technologies such as ammonia under consideration. The company has increasingly emphasized having multiple fuel options because shipowners face uncertainty over future fuel supplies, costs and global emissions regulations.
The most defensible interpretation is that Maersk is treating fuel choice as a risk-management problem. With no single fuel clearly winning on supply, cost and regulatory acceptance, keeping several pathways open is a rational response, and having ships that can run on more than one alcohol supports that strategy.
The source material does not disclose the volume of ethanol bunkered, the price paid, or any cost comparison with methanol or conventional fuel. It also says nothing about the lifecycle emissions of this particular ethanol, the engine's performance on 100% ethanol, or any commitment to repeat or scale the operation. Without these details, conclusions about economics, emissions benefit or scalability would be speculation.
The signals worth following are whether Maersk repeats ethanol bunkering and in which ports, whether regulators clarify how ethanol is treated as a marine fuel, whether other carriers or suppliers follow with alcohol bunkering, and whether Maersk's newbuilding orders come to reflect the broader fuel mix it describes.
The Houston bunkering is a real operational milestone, but Maersk presents it as a learning exercise rather than a change of strategy. Its significance lies in showing that an alcohol-capable ship can be fueled with a second alcohol through a commercial supply chain, and in reinforcing a multi-fuel approach to an uncertain regulatory and supply landscape.

articles.title: Rio Tinto And Shougang Commission Industrial Scale CCS Trial
articles.raw_title: Rio Tinto And Shougang Commission Industrial Scale CCS Trial
articles.snippet: China steelmaker Shougang has worked with Rio Tinto to commission an industrial scale carbon capture trial at its Jingtang steelmaking complex.
articles.text:
Chinese steelmaker Shougang has successfully built and commissioned an industrial scale carbon capture facility to capture blast furnace gas produced during the production of crude steel at its Jingtang steelmaking complex in Caofeidian, in China's Tangshan steelmaking heartland.
The achievement follows scarcely three months since Shougang’s bioethanol producing subsidiary Shougang Lanzatech announced the completion of the world’s first demonstration project for the biosynthesis of anhydrous ethanol from offgases from a blast furnace, its Hebei Shouland Phase II project.
Jingtang blast furnace carbon capture trial
The trial facility will have the capacity to process up to 3,000 cubic metres of blast furnace gas per hour, and to capture up to 10,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide each year.
Shougang Group Vice President Zhu Guosen comments: “This achievement represents an important milestone for blast furnace decarbonisation and provides valuable demonstration value for reducing emissions in the conventional steelmaking route.
“The project has effectively addressed key challenges associated with carbon reduction in the blast furnace process… Looking ahead, we will continue to optimise the technology, advance the utilisation of captured carbon resources, and contribute to the green and low-carbon transformation of the steel industry.”
The newly built facility follows a smaller-scale blast furnace carbon capture facility commissioned in 2024, as part of the phased technology development program under the partnership. Using waste heat from the existing operations has the potential to further reduce carbon capture costs.
Rio Tinto Iron Ore Sales and Marketing Vice President Ramona Sim says: “This milestone is an important step in our 30-year relationship with Shougang and our work together to find practical ways to reduce emissions from steelmaking.”
“Steelmakers are exploring a range of technologies to lower emissions from existing blast furnace operations, and carbon capture and utilisation could play a key role as these technologies continue to develop.”
Rio Tinto and Shougang are also exploring ways to use the captured CO₂, including converting it into syngas that can be recycled back into the steelmaking process, reducing the amount of new carbon needed to make steel.
However, the Shougang Group has also been actively investigating the possibilities offered by using captured carbon-rich offgases as feedstock for bioethanol production.
Carbon capture as bioethanol feedstock
Shougang has been investigating the possibility of recycling captured carbon at its Jingtang steel mill in Caofeidian since 2018, when it started up bioethanol production using captured carbon from the steel mill as feedstock.
Shougang established a China-based joint venture, Shougang Lanzatech, with its US technology partner, LanzaTech. Shougang Lanzatech has continued to commercialise its products, having initially produced synthetic vehicle fuel. In late September 2026, Shougang Lanzatech exhibited its products at the 2026 China Metallurgical Exhibition.
Meanwhile, in June 2026, Shougang Lanzatech announced that it had achieved a technical breakthrough, completing the world’s first demonstration project for the biosynthesis of anhydrous ethanol from offgases from a blast furnace. The anhydrous ethanol was produced with a concentration of 99.9%. Shougang Lanzatech also added that it had entered commercial operations.
- CCUS can be retrofitted to existing power and industrial plants, which could otherwise still be significant emitters by 2050
- CCUS can tackle emissions in hard to abate sectors, such as in the production of cement, iron and steel or chemicals, and to produce synthetic fuels for long-distance transportation
- In many cases, CCUS products, such as synthetic fuels, are combusted and the carbon contained within them is released to the atmosphere as CO2.
- Applications other than synthetic fuels are being considered; these include oxygenated compounds (polycarbonate, urethane, etc.), biomass-derived chemicals and commodity chemicals (such as bioethanol)
- The reuse of CO2 to reduce industrial emissions will enable the further development of CO2 capture technology without the deployment of CO2 transportation infrastructure
Meet Rio Tinto's decarbonisation partners
Caterpillar - Rio Tinto is partnering with Caterpillar to help develop 220-tonne zero-emission autonomous haul trucks. Rio Tinto is also working with Caterpillar on validating its emerging zero-emissions technology.
Prysmian - Rio Tinto and Prysmian announced that they would partner in March 2026 on an industrial trial to produce low-carbon aluminium cables designed for the rapidly growing data centre market to help customers reduce the carbon footprint of critical IT infrastructure.
Shougang - Rio Tinto has been collaborating with Chinese steelmaker Shougang as part of a plan to develop carbon capture technology to reduce emissions from blast furnace route steelmaking.
US Department of Energy - Rio Tinto is participating in a three-year project as a part of a program funded by the US Department of Energy’s Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy (ARPA-E). The project is exploring the carbon storage potential of the Tamarack nickel joint venture in central Minnesota.

articles.title: Dosen Polinela Kembangkan Pakan Ternak dari Limbah Padi untuk Tekan Emisi Metana - radarlampung.disway.id
articles.raw_title: Dosen Polinela Kembangkan Pakan Ternak dari Limbah Padi untuk Tekan Emisi Metana - radarlampung.disway.id
articles.snippet: Limbah pertanian berupa jerami dan sekam padi dikembangkan menjadi bahan baku pakan ternak yang berpotensi menekan emisi gas metana.
articles.text:
RADARLAMPUNG.CO.ID – Limbah pertanian berupa jerami dan sekam padi dikembangkan menjadi bahan baku pakan ternak yang berpotensi menekan emisi gas metana.
Inovasi ini tengah diteliti tim dosen Politeknik Negeri Lampung (Polinela) melalui kombinasi teknologi amoniasi jerami dan suplementasi biochar sekam padi.
Penelitian tersebut dipimpin Efrilia Tri Wahyu Utami, M.Pt., dengan fokus mengembangkan pakan ruminansia yang lebih efisien, ekonomis, dan ramah lingkungan di tengah tantangan perubahan iklim.
 Proses amoniasi jerami.---Sumber Foto : Efrilia Tri Wahyu Utami, M.Pt. Dosen Prodi Teknologi Pakan Ternak- Polinela.---
Efrilia menjelaskan, jerami padi memiliki potensi besar sebagai pakan alternatif karena ketersediaannya melimpah dan harganya relatif murah.
BACA JUGA:Tiga Mahasiswa Teknokrat Tembus 15 Besar CTF Compfest 2026
Namun, kandungan lignin dan silika yang tinggi membuat jerami sulit dicerna sehingga nilai nutrisinya masih rendah.
Melalui teknologi amoniasi menggunakan urea, struktur jerami dapat diurai untuk meningkatkan kandungan nitrogen dan kecernaannya. Meski demikian, peningkatan kecernaan serat juga perlu diimbangi dengan upaya mengendalikan produksi gas metana dari fermentasi rumen.
 Proses amoniasi jerami.---Sumber Foto : Efrilia Tri Wahyu Utami, M.Pt. Dosen Prodi Teknologi Pakan Ternak- Polinela.---
"Teknologi amoniasi terbukti efektif meningkatkan kualitas nutrisi jerami padi dengan memutus ikatan lignoselulosa dan menaikkan kandungan nitrogen," ujar Efrilia mewakili tim peneliti, Rabu 30 September 2026.
Untuk melengkapi teknologi tersebut, tim mengombinasikan jerami teramoniasi dengan biochar berbahan sekam padi.
BACA JUGA:Ukir Sejarah Tingkat Internasional, PLTU Sumsel-8 Raih Zhan Tianyou Award 2026
Material karbon berpori ini berpotensi menjadi media bagi pertumbuhan mikroba rumen yang menguntungkan sekaligus mendukung transfer elektron antarspesies atau Direct Interspecies Electron Transfer (DIET).
Mekanisme tersebut diharapkan dapat mengarahkan proses fermentasi sehingga mengurangi pembentukan metana tanpa mengganggu pencernaan pakan.
Sebab, gas metana tidak hanya berkontribusi terhadap pemanasan global, tetapi juga menyebabkan hilangnya energi pakan sebesar 2–12 persen.

articles.title: BPTU-HPT Indrapuri Buka Ruang Kritik untuk Perbaiki Layanan Peternakan
articles.raw_title: BPTU-HPT Indrapuri Buka Ruang Kritik untuk Perbaiki Layanan Peternakan
articles.snippet: MASAKINI.CO – Balai Pembibitan Ternak Unggul dan Hijauan Pakan Ternak (BPTU-HPT) Indrapuri membuka ruang bagi masyarakat dan pemangku kepentingan untuk...
articles.text:
MASAKINI.CO – Balai Pembibitan Ternak Unggul dan Hijauan Pakan Ternak (BPTU-HPT) Indrapuri membuka ruang bagi masyarakat dan pemangku kepentingan untuk menyampaikan kritik serta masukan terhadap layanan peternakan yang diberikan.
Hal itu disampaikan Ketua Panitia Forum Konsultasi Publik BPTU-HPT Indrapuri, drh. Leliana, dalam Forum Konsultasi Publik Standar Pelayanan Publik Tahun 2026, Rabu (30/9/2026).
Menurut Leliana, forum tersebut menjadi bagian dari upaya BPTU-HPT Indrapuri mengevaluasi sekaligus meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan. Ia menegaskan, pelayanan publik yang baik membutuhkan organisasi yang mau mendengar dan terus melakukan pembenahan.
“Karena kami yakin bahwa pelayanan publik yang baik tidak lahir dari organisasi yang merasa sudah sempurna, tetapi dari organisasi yang ingin dan mau mendengar dan terus berbenah,” ujar Leliana.
Ia mengatakan setiap masukan yang disampaikan masyarakat akan menjadi bahan evaluasi dan perbaikan pelayanan sesuai dengan kewenangan serta kemampuan organisasi.
“Dengan demikian, kritik bukan ancaman tapi bahan perbaikan” katanya.
Leliana menjelaskan, BPTU-HPT Indrapuri memiliki sejumlah layanan yang dapat dimanfaatkan masyarakat dan pemangku kepentingan, mulai dari penyediaan bibit unggul Sapi Aceh hingga hijauan pakan ternak.
Layanan bibit unggul Sapi Aceh tidak hanya diarahkan untuk menyediakan ternak, tetapi juga mendukung pelestarian dan pengembangan Sapi Aceh sebagai plasma nutfah yang menjadi bagian dari kekayaan genetika Indonesia.
Selain bibit, BPTU-HPT Indrapuri menyediakan hijauan pakan ternak. Menurut Leliana, produktivitas ternak tidak hanya ditentukan oleh kualitas bibit, tetapi juga ketersediaan pakan yang berkualitas.
BPTU-HPT Indrapuri juga menyediakan layanan kompos dan pupuk organik dengan memanfaatkan limbah peternakan agar memiliki nilai guna.
Layanan lainnya mencakup bimbingan teknis, penelitian, praktik kerja lapangan (PKL), magang, Kuliah Kerja Profesi (KKP), koasistensi, serta kunjungan eduwisata, fotografi dan videografi.
“BPTU-HPT Indrapuri bukan hanya tempat pengembangan bibit ternak tapi ruang belajar, ruang berbagi pengetahuan, ruang penelitian, ruang kolaborasi, dan ruang pelayanan bagi masyarakat,” ujarnya.
Keunggulan yang Dikembangkan BPTU-HPT
Kepala BPTU-HPT Indrapuri, Dayat, mengatakan salah satu keunggulan yang dikembangkan di BPTU-HPT Indrapuri adalah kemampuan ternak beradaptasi terhadap kondisi pakan.
Ia menyebut wilayah Indrapuri berada pada zona musim 5 dengan periode musim hujan relatif singkat, yakni sekitar tujuh hingga sembilan dasarian yang umumnya berlangsung pada Oktober hingga Desember.
Setelah periode tersebut, wilayah Indrapuri memasuki musim kemarau. Namun, Dayat mengatakan kondisi padang penggembalaan di BPTU-HPT Indrapuri tetap diupayakan terjaga sehingga ketersediaan pakan dapat mendukung produktivitas ternak.
“Jadi zona musim 5 itu tujuh sampai sembilan dasarian saja untuk waktu musim hujan. Itu jatuh di bulan Oktober, November, dan Desember. Setelah bulan itu kami memasuki masa kemarau,” kata Dayat.
Menurutnya, kondisi hijauan yang tetap terjaga menjadi salah satu indikator yang ingin terus dikembangkan BPTU-HPT Indrapuri pada 2027.
Ia mengatakan pengelolaan tersebut didukung teknologi dan berbagai inovasi untuk meningkatkan pelayanan serta produktivitas budidaya ternak.

articles.title: Peternak Bluto Kesulitan Mendapatkan Hijauan Pakan
articles.raw_title: Peternak Bluto Kesulitan Mendapatkan Hijauan Pakan
articles.snippet: Para penggembala sapi di Kecamatan Bluto, Kabupaten Sumenep, mulai kesulitan mendapatkan hijauan untuk pakan ternak. Kondisi kemarau membuat rumput segar...
articles.text:
Peternak Bluto Kesulitan Mendapatkan Hijauan Pakan
- 29 Sep 2026 15:38 WIB
RRI.CO.ID, Sumenep - Para penggembala sapi di Kecamatan Bluto, Kabupaten Sumenep, mulai kesulitan mendapatkan hijauan untuk pakan ternak. Kondisi kemarau membuat rumput segar semakin sulit ditemukan di lahan yang biasa menjadi lokasi mencari pakan.
Salah seorang peternak, Samsul, mengatakan, dalam kondisi normal dirinya hanya membutuhkan waktu sekitar setengah jam untuk mendapatkan hijauan di ladang yang dimilikinya.
Namun, saat ini waktu yang dibutuhkan jauh lebih lama. Samsul mengaku harus mencari hingga sedikitnya dua jam untuk mendapatkan pakan yang cukup bagi ternaknya.
“Sekarang sulit cari hijauan, jadi walaupun kering kita jadikan pakan,” katanya.
Menurut Samsul, persediaan pakan cadangan yang sebelumnya disiapkan untuk menghadapi musim kemarau juga mulai menipis. Saat musim panen padi, warga biasanya mengumpulkan jerami untuk dikeringkan dan disimpan sebagai pakan ternak.
“Kalau tidak ada pakan cadangan yang disimpan, kita kelimpungan,” ujarnya.
Selain menyimpan jerami kering, Samsul juga menyiapkan batang atau pohon jagung yang telah dikeringkan sebagai pakan alternatif. Persediaan tersebut digunakan untuk menjaga kebutuhan pakan sapi tetap terpenuhi ketika hijauan segar semakin sulit diperoleh.(RIA)

articles.title: NTB Belajar Program Desaku Maju Lampung, Ini yang Dipelajari
articles.raw_title: NTB Belajar Program Desaku Maju Lampung, Ini yang Dipelajari
articles.snippet: Pemprov NTB studi tiru Program Desaku Maju Lampung untuk mempelajari pengembangan ekonomi desa dari produksi hingga proses hilirisasi.
articles.text:
LAMPUNG - Pemerintah Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Barat (NTB) melakukan studi tiru Program Desaku Maju Pemerintah Provinsi Lampung untuk mempelajari pengembangan ekosistem ekonomi desa yang melibatkan berbagai perangkat daerah.
Kunjungan rombongan Pemprov NTB tersebut diterima Pemerintah Provinsi Lampung di Ruang Rapat Utama Kantor Gubernur Lampung, Selasa (29/9/2026).
Studi tiru tersebut menjadi kesempatan bagi Pemprov NTB untuk melihat secara langsung bagaimana Program Desaku Maju mengintegrasikan berbagai program perangkat daerah, mulai dari sektor pertanian, pengolahan hasil produksi, peternakan, perikanan, hingga pengembangan sumber daya manusia di desa.
Sekretaris Daerah Provinsi Lampung Marindo Kurniawan menjelaskan Program Desaku Maju dibangun sebagai sebuah ekosistem ekonomi desa yang melibatkan program dari berbagai perangkat daerah.
Baca juga: Pekon Tanjung Raya di Lampung Barat Jadi Percontohan Program Desaku Maju
Produksi hingga Hilirisasi Diintegrasikan di Desa
Marindo mengatakan Dinas Ketahanan Pangan, Tanaman Pangan dan Hortikultura (KPTPH) memiliki peran pada sektor hulu, sementara Dinas Perindustrian dan Perdagangan berperan dalam proses hilirisasi.
Salah satu dukungan di sektor pertanian dilakukan melalui program pupuk hayati cair yang diproduksi Dinas KPTPH dan diberikan secara gratis kepada masyarakat.
Sementara pada sektor hilirisasi, Dinas Perindustrian dan Perdagangan menjalankan program pengadaan dryer, Rice Milling Unit (RMU), serta pakan ternak dan pakan ikan.
Menurut Marindo, keberadaan fasilitas tersebut diarahkan agar pengolahan hasil produksi dapat dilakukan di desa sehingga nilai tambah komoditas tidak seluruhnya keluar dari wilayah desa.
Salah satu contohnya adalah hasil produksi padi yang dapat diolah hingga menjadi beras di desa.
Baca juga: Strategi Pemprov Lampung Tekan Pengangguran, dari Pelatihan hingga Program Desaku Maju
Libatkan Banyak Perangkat Daerah
Marindo menjelaskan Program Desaku Maju tidak hanya berfokus pada sektor pertanian dan hilirisasi, tetapi melibatkan sejumlah perangkat daerah sesuai dengan bidang masing-masing.
Dinas Pemberdayaan Masyarakat dan Desa berperan mengawal pelaksanaan ekosistem program di desa.
Sementara Dinas Tenaga Kerja mengampu program vokasi bagi anak muda di desa. Program tersebut diarahkan untuk meningkatkan kualitas sumber daya manusia agar mampu mendukung terbentuknya ekosistem ekonomi desa.
Dinas Kelautan dan Perikanan juga berperan dalam pengembangan sektor perikanan, termasuk penyediaan pakan ikan.
Pada sektor peternakan, konsep hilirisasi dilakukan dengan memanfaatkan hasil pertanian sebagai bahan baku pakan ternak.
Jagung, misalnya, dapat dikeringkan menggunakan dryer sebelum kemudian diolah menjadi pakan ternak.
Bappeda Susun Perencanaan Program
Marindo menambahkan, perencanaan Program Desaku Maju dilakukan oleh Bappeda Provinsi Lampung, mulai dari kajian, analisis, hingga mekanisme penganggaran.
Sementara pelaksanaan program dilakukan oleh masing-masing perangkat daerah sesuai dengan tugas dan sektor yang ditangani.
Program Desaku Maju juga diintegrasikan dengan program lain yang dimiliki Pemprov Lampung, seperti desa wisata dan budaya serta desa ekspor.
Dengan integrasi tersebut, pengembangan desa diarahkan tidak hanya pada peningkatan produksi, tetapi juga pengolahan, pemasaran, pengembangan sumber daya manusia, serta pembukaan akses ekonomi yang lebih luas.
Baca juga: Program Desaku Maju Jadi Faktor Lampung Raih Terbaik 3 Nasional PPD 2025 dari Bappenas RI
NTB: Kami Datang untuk Belajar
Asisten Pemerintahan dan Kesejahteraan Rakyat Provinsi NTB Fathul Gani menyampaikan apresiasi atas sambutan Pemerintah Provinsi Lampung terhadap rombongan studi tiru.
Ia mengatakan kunjungan tersebut dilakukan untuk melihat secara langsung pelaksanaan Program Desaku Maju di Lampung.
“Kami datang untuk belajar, inovasi hebat Desaku Maju,” ujarnya.
Fathul Gani menjelaskan NTB juga memiliki program Desa Berdaya yang terdiri atas Desa Berdaya Tematik dan Desa Berdaya Transformatif.
Menurutnya, terdapat kemiripan antara konsep Desa Berdaya di NTB dengan Program Desaku Maju di Lampung sehingga dapat menjadi bahan pertukaran pengalaman bagi kedua daerah.
Kunjungan tersebut juga merupakan tindak lanjut dari perbincangan antara pimpinan kedua daerah. Pemprov NTB kemudian mengirimkan delegasi untuk mempelajari secara langsung pelaksanaan Program Desaku Maju di Lampung.
Fathul Gani turut mengundang Pemerintah Provinsi Lampung untuk melakukan kunjungan balasan ke NTB.
Ia berharap pertukaran pengalaman tersebut dapat memberikan manfaat bagi kedua pemerintah provinsi dalam mengembangkan program pembangunan desa.
Baca juga: Program Desaku Maju, Produksi Padi Wonomarto Lampung Utara Naik 30 Persen
Delegasi NTB Kunjungi Desa Wonomarto
Setelah pemaparan konsep Program Desaku Maju oleh Kepala Bappeda Provinsi Lampung, rombongan Pemprov NTB dijadwalkan melihat secara langsung implementasi program tersebut di Desa Wonomarto, Kabupaten Lampung Utara.
Desa Wonomarto menjadi salah satu desa percontohan dalam pelaksanaan Program Desaku Maju.
Kunjungan lapangan tersebut menjadi bagian dari rangkaian studi tiru untuk memberikan gambaran langsung mengenai penerapan konsep pengembangan ekosistem ekonomi desa yang telah dijalankan Pemerintah Provinsi Lampung.

articles.title: Kekeringan Melanda Desa Kami, Tak Ada Rumput untuk Kambing Tuminah
articles.raw_title: Kekeringan Melanda Desa Kami, Tak Ada Rumput untuk Kambing Tuminah
articles.snippet: Setiap kemarau tiba, Tuminah warga Gunung Kidul, mencemaskan kambingnya yang tak bisa makan rumput dan minum yang cukup akibat kekeringan.
articles.text:
Tuminah selalu merasa sedih ketika musim kemarau datang. Wajahnya kerap murung.
Tak hanya warga yang harus mengirit air, kambing-kambing nya juga.
Tinggal di Gunungkidul, salah satu kawasan di Yogyakarta yang kondisi tanahnya tandus dan kering ketika musim kemarau tiba, membuat Tuminah harus berhitung dengan cermat untuk menyisihkan air dan rumput segar.
Tuminah adalah perempuan janda yang hidup dengan ditemani kambing-kambingnya.
Mbok Tuminah- kami memanggilnya begitu- hidup bersama 3 ekor kambing. Nama kambingnya Belang, Hitam, dan Putih. Ia merawat 3 kambingnya seperti anaknya sendiri, diberi makan dan minum agar mereka bisa hidup sehat.
Mbok Tuminah tinggal di Dusun Wuni, Giricahyo, Purwosari, Gunungkidul, Yogyakarta. Ia masih bekerja sebagai buruh tani walau umurnya sudah lansia. Sehari-hari ia bekerja sebagai buruh di ladang, dan aktif di Kelompok Wanita Tani (KWT) di Dusun Wuni.
Dulu Tuminah hidup dengan kakaknya, namun setelah kakaknya meninggal, ia hidup sendiri ditemani kambing- kambingnya.
Setiap pagi, Mbok Tuminah mencari rumput untuk pakan ternak kambingnya. Setelah pulang dari mencari rumput untuk 3 ekor kambingnya, ia bekerja sebagai buruh cangkul di ladang tetangga. Upah buruh cangkul sebesar Rp. 30.000 rupiah perhari, namun ini tetap membuatnya semangat, walau dengan upah yang sangat minim untuk kebutuhan sehari-hari
Tahun ini kemarau panjang terjadi, dari Juni sampai September 2026. Langit Giricahyo belum juga mengeluarkan hujan selama 3 bulan. Dulu tiap musim kemarau ia bisa mencari rumput di kebun, ada rumput liar, daun singkong, daun nangka yang bisa ia masak dan ia sisihkan untuk kambing- kambingnya. Sekarang kebun tersebut sudah gersang, tanah retak, rumput mati belum sempat tumbuh lagi akibat musim kemarau panjang. Kekeringan ini akhirnya berakibat bagi ketiga kambingnya, mereka jadi jarang mendapatkan rumput, air pun juga terbatas.
Baca juga: Ceritaku Perempuan Petani Milenial, Tak Kapok Tanam Cabai Meski Kemarau Panjang Menghantam
Di Yogyakarta, Gunungkidul termasuk kawasan tandus, karena daerahnya didominasi oleh perbukitan dan pegunungan kapur (karst). Sebagian besar wilayah ini terdiri dari batuan gamping yang minim air, sehingga sering mengalami kekeringan saat musim kemarau. Kondisi lahan yang kering, membuat masyarakat terbiasa mengolah singkong menjadi makanan sehari-hari. Walaupun saat ini sudah ada inovasi lahan kritis dan ada bantuan air, namun jika musim kemarau tiba, tanah-tanah disini cepat kering.
Biasanya, pagi-pagi jam 5 Mbok Tuminah sudah bangun, bukan buat masak, tapi buat mengantri air. Truk tangki datang seminggu sekali. Biasanya 1 Kepala Keluarga (KK) mendapatkan 4 jerigen air. Air ini dipakai buat masak, buat minum, buat wudhu, juga buat minum kambingnya.
Kondisi kekeringan di Gunungkidul membuat masyarakat disana harus siap dengan persediaan air. Ada air bersih dari truk tangki yang datang, ada juga air hujan yang disimpan. Penyimpanan air hujan menjadi hal yang tak terelakkan di beberapa wilayah di Gunungkidul karena lahan disana yang sangat kering, sehingga air hujan sering digunakan untuk kebutuhan sehari-hari.
Tiga kambing menjadi punya arti buat mbok Tuminah, dalam situasi kekeringan seperti ini, ia selalu murung ketika memikirkan kambingnya.
Kambing-kambing mbok Tuminah ini ia dapatkan dari arisan kambing yang ia dapat dari KWT. Ia juga pernah mendapatkan arisan kambing yang didanai dari Yakkum Emergency Unit (YEU). Lalu si Hitam sama si Putih ia beli dari hasil jual jagung hasil panen. Mbok Tuminah menjadi anggota KWT sudah masuk 8 tahun ini.
Tapi sekarang cari makan kambingnya ini susah. Ia harus berjalan kaki 2 kilometer ke bukit, mencari daun-daun kering yang masih hijau sedikit. Pulangnya ia baru bisa membawa sekarung daun kering. Punggungnya sering merasa pegal.
“Maaf ya Le, tahun ini makanmu jadi kurang,” bisiknya sambil mengusap kepala kambingnya, si Putih.
Daun-daun yang menjadi kering karena musim kemarau dan kekeringan di sana membuat kambing-kambing harus memakan daun kering seadanya.
“Paling berat pas air buat minum kambing habis duluan.”
Ia kemudian berusaha menyisihkan air dari cucian beras, yang diberikan ke kambingnya pakai ember kecil. Tetangga nya sering bilang agar ia menjual kambingnya agar tak merepotkannya.
“Bu, dijual saja kambingnya, daripada mati kelaparan.”
Saya lihat, ia cuma senyum-senyum saja, “Nek dijual terus aku dolan karo sopo (kalau kambingnya dijual, nanti aku main sama siapa).”
Suatu malam si Hitam lemas, nggak mau makan. Mbok Tuminah begadang, menyalakan lampu senter, menyuapinya dengan air gula pakai sendok.
“Kuat ya Le, nenek karo kowe wes sumpah urip, bareng-bareng.” (kuat ya kamu, aku sudah bersumpah jika kita akan hidup bersama-sama).
Musim kemarau ini jelas membuat nya kesulitan mencari pakan kambingnya. Setiap pagi jam 7 setelah mengantri air, ia sudah ke ladang mencari pakan kambingnya. Karena adanya kemarau panjang ini, ia memberi pakan kambingnya dengan daun kering, yaitu daun melinjo.
Pagi ini tiba-tiba saya melihat kambingnya Mbok Tuminah sudah bertambah menjadi 5 ekor kambing.
Besoknya ketika pertemuan KWT, tiba-tiba ada petugas penyuluh datang. Mereka lalu mengajarkan cara membuat pakan ternak fermentasi dari jerami dan dedak untuk hewan, juga mengajarkan bagaimana caranya agar tempat minum tetes untuk hewan agar airnya tidak terbuang. Mbok Tuminah mencatat semua informasi dari penyuluh itu di buku tulis, tangannya gemetar tapi matanya semangat.
Sebulan kemudian keajaiban kecil datang. Hujan turun 20 menit, tidak begitu lebat, tapi cukup buat menampung air di ember. Saya lihat dari jauh, ia bersama 3 kambingnya basah kuyup di halaman. Mbok Tuminah tertawa, si Belang melompat-lompat.
Kemarin mbok Tuminah juga cerita bahwa ia berencana menjual kambingnya, tapi harga kambing sekarang masih murah, jadi batal tidak jadi menjual kambingnya. Sebenarnya Mbok Tum sangat membutuhkan uang untuk kebutuhan sehari-harinya, walau ia tetap bersyukur, karena setiap hari ia masih dapat uang dari pekerjaannya sebagai buruh cangkul, uangnya bisa dipergunakan untuk kebutuhan sehari hari. Jadi niat untuk menjual kambing masih bisa diurungkan.
Setelah mendapat penyuluhan dari petugas itu, sekarang Mbok Tuminah sudah bisa membuat pakan ternak sendiri dari fermentasi daun kering dan dedak, dan akhirnya kebutuhan pakan untuk kambing nya terpenuhi.
Aku merasa senang bertetangga dengan mbok Tuminah, hidupnya sangat sederhana bersama kambing-kambingnya.
Terimakasih mbok Tuminah sudah mengajarkan soal kesetiaan dan cinta pada kami- untuk merawat binatang secara tulus.
Editor: Luviana Ariyanti

articles.title: Kemarau Panjang Ancam Pakan Ternak di KBB, Dinas Dorong Penguatan Cadangan Pakan
articles.raw_title: Kemarau Panjang Ancam Pakan Ternak di KBB, Dinas Dorong Penguatan Cadangan Pakan
articles.snippet: Bandung Barat, hariandialog.co.id – Kemarau berkepanjangan sejak Juni 2026 menekan ketersediaan hijauan pakan ternak ruminansia di Kabupaten Bandung Barat...
articles.text:
Bandung Barat, hariandialog.co.id – Kemarau berkepanjangan sejak Juni 2026 menekan ketersediaan hijauan pakan ternak ruminansia di Kabupaten Bandung Barat (KBB). Produksi kebun rumput dilaporkan merosot hingga 30 persen, memaksa sebagian peternak mencari rumput hingga ke luar daerah seperti Subang dan Sumedang, serta beralih ke jerami padi kering..
Kepala Dinas Perikanan dan Peternakan KBB, drh. Wiwin Aprianti, M.Si., mengimbau para peternak agar tidak menunggu ketersediaan rumput kritis. Peternak didorong untuk mulai membangun ketahanan pakan dengan mengolah bahan lokal menjadi pakan awetan, seperti silase atau hay, serta memanfaatkan pakan alternatif seperti ampas tahu dan konsentrat.
Berikut adalah pokok-pokok penting dari situasi di lapangan:
Populasi Terdampak: Meliputi 5.960 ekor sapi potong, 26.717 ekor sapi perah, 14.744 ekor kambing, dan 184.123 ekor domba yang tersebar di berbagai sentra peternakan seperti Lembang dan Cisarua.
Lonjakan Harga Pakan: Harga tebon jagung naik menjadi Rp900/kg dan rumput odot menjadi Rp900/kg akibat keterbatasan stok.
Langkah Antisipasi Dinas: Memperkuat pemantauan melalui UPTD dan penyuluh serta menggalakkan edukasi pengolahan pakan awetan dan manajemen cadangan air minum bagi ternak.
Peternak yang mengalami kesulitan pakan atau penurunan kondisi ternak diimbau untuk segera berkoordinasi dengan penyuluh atau petugas peternakan setempat. (Nagon)

articles.title: Indeks Kepercayaan Industri September 2026 Melambat Jadi 51,93
articles.raw_title: Indeks Kepercayaan Industri September 2026 Melambat Jadi 51,93
articles.snippet: Kemenperin mencatat Indeks Kepercayaan Industri manufaktur nasional pada September 2026 berada di level 51,93 atau melambat 0,37 poin.
articles.text:
Indeks Kepercayaan Industri September 2026 Melambat Jadi 51,93
Aktivitas industri manufaktur nasional pada September 2026 tetap berada dalam fase ekspansi dengan Indeks Kepercayaan Industri sebesar 51,93, meski melambat 0,37 poin dibandingkan Agustus 2026 yang mencapai 52,30, sebagaimana dilansir dari Investor Daily pada Rabu (30/9/2026). Kementerian Perindustrian melaporkan bahwa capaian tersebut ditopang oleh 15 subsektor yang mengalami ekspansi dari total 23 subsektor industri pengolahan yang dianalisis. Kelompok subsektor yang ekspansif ini menyumbang 84,4 persen terhadap produk domestik bruto industri pengolahan nonmigas pada triwulan II-2026.
Industri minuman serta industri alat angkutan lainnya tercatat sebagai dua subsektor dengan nilai indeks tertinggi pada periode tersebut. Sementara itu, delapan subsektor lainnya mengalami kontraksi, antara lain industri kulit, kayu, kertas, karet dan plastik, komputer, elektronik dan optik, peralatan listrik, serta mesin dan perlengkapan.
Dari sisi variabel pembentuk indeks, komponen pesanan menguat menjadi 53,40 dari sebelumnya 53,13 pada Agustus. Di sisi lain, indeks produksi berada di level 53,78 atau turun 1,32 poin, sedangkan indeks persediaan masih tertahan di zona kontraksi pada level 45,45.
Berdasarkan orientasi pasarnya, kelompok industri berorientasi ekspor membukukan angka 52,60, sedangkan sektor yang berfokus pada pasar domestik mencatatkan angka 50,94. Kedua kategori tersebut masih berada di zona ekspansif kendati pertumbuhannya melambat jika dibandingkan dengan bulan sebelumnya. Kementerian Perindustrian menilai dinamika ini menunjukkan perlunya menjaga keseimbangan antara pasar domestik dan ekspor. Langkah tersebut dinilai krusial guna menghadapi tantangan persaingan produk impor, kenaikan biaya produksi, serta dinamika perdagangan global.
